text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Could you please describe the newborn's presenting symptoms and any relevant details from the birth or family history?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Doctor
text: I notice the mother had no prenatal care; does the newborn show any skin lesions, particularly a "blueberry muffin" rash, or signs of jaundice? Also, are there any visible signs of organ enlargement like hepatosplenomegaly or cataracts on initial inspection?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of a continuous heart murmur, "blueberry muffin" rash, cataracts, and hearing loss is highly suggestive of congenital rubella syndrome. Given the lack of prenatal care and immunization history, I will proceed with confirmation. REQUEST TEST: Rubella IgM Antibody. REQUEST TEST: Congenital Rubella PCR.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Rubella IgM Antibody: Positive. Congenital Rubella PCR: Positive (inferred from clinical confirmation context). Additional findings confirming Congenital Rubella Syndrome: Patent ductus arteriosus (Echocardiogram), Bilateral congenital cataracts (Ophthalmologic Consult), and Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss (Hearing Test).

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical findings of a continuous heart murmur (patent ductus arteriosus), "blueberry muffin" rash, bilateral cataracts, and sensorineural hearing loss, combined with the positive Rubella IgM and PCR results, confirm the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Rubella Syndrome.
